components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 你今晚有空吗?我们能聊聊吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ jīnwǎn yǒukòng ma? Wǒmen néng liáoliao ma?
example.english: Are you free tonight? Can we talk?
example.fact: 有空 literally means "to have (有) emptiness, free space (空)" — treating free time as an open, unoccupied slot in one's schedule, much like English "I have an opening." Its negation is simply 没有空, usually contracted to 没空.

examples.hanzi: 你明天有空吗？一起吃个饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān yǒukòng ma? Yìqǐ chī ge fàn ba.
examples.english: Are you free tomorrow? Let's have a meal together.

examples.hanzi: 等我有空，就去看你。
examples.pinyin: Děng wǒ yǒukòng, jiù qù kàn nǐ.
examples.english: When I have time, I'll come see you.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.

example.hanzi: 请深呼吸。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shēn hūxī.
example.english: Please take a deep breath.
example.fact: 呼 is exhaling, and 吸 is inhaling, together 呼吸 (breathing). 呼 also means to call out: 招呼 (to greet; 打招呼 means to say hello) and 称呼 (a form of address).

examples.hanzi: 他大声呼救。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàshēng hūjiù.
examples.english: He called loudly for help.

examples.hanzi: 见面时,他们互相打招呼。
examples.pinyin: Jiànmiàn shí, tāmen hùxiāng dǎ zhāohu.
examples.english: When they met, they greeted each other.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: a spoken pronoun.
自 (zì) is only a loose sound clue for zán.

example.hanzi: 咱们一起走吧。
example.pinyin: Zánmen yìqǐ zǒu ba.
example.english: Let's go together.
example.fact: 咱们 is the inclusive 'we', which always includes the listener, unlike 我们, which may leave them out. It is typical of northern and Beijing speech and sounds friendly and close.

examples.hanzi: 咱们明天几点见面?
examples.pinyin: Zánmen míngtiān jǐ diǎn jiànmiàn?
examples.english: What time shall we meet tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 咱家今天晚上吃饺子。
examples.pinyin: Zán jiā jīntiān wǎnshang chī jiǎozi.
examples.english: We're having dumplings at our place tonight.

components.note: 白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的营业额超过一百万。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de yíngyè'é chāoguò yì bǎiwàn.
example.english: This company's revenue exceeds one million.
example.fact: The Chinese numbering system groups by four digits (万 "ten-thousand," 亿 "hundred-million") rather than English's three-digit groupings. 百万 ("hundred-万") is one of the few big numbers with a word matching Western "million," while native counting more naturally jumps straight from 万 to 亿.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有两百万人口。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu liǎng bǎiwàn rénkǒu.
examples.english: This city has a population of two million.

examples.hanzi: 他中了一百万的大奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhòng le yì bǎiwàn de dà jiǎng.
examples.english: He won a million-yuan jackpot.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood, as in 桌, 板; a ladder was a wooden structure.
弟 (dì) — near sound — 梯 is tī; 弟 also sounds out 第 dì and 递 dì.

example.hanzi: 请走楼梯,电梯坏了。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zǒu lóutī, diàntī huài le.
example.english: Please take the stairs, the elevator is broken.
example.fact: 楼梯 and 电梯 ("elevator," literally "electric-梯") both end in 梯, a character built around 木 ("wood") depicting a ladder. The same root distinguishes a plain staircase ("building-ladder") from its modern electric counterpart just by swapping the first character.

examples.hanzi: 这座楼梯很陡，小心点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lóutī hěn dǒu, xiǎoxīn diǎn.
examples.english: This staircase is steep, so be careful.

examples.hanzi: 我在楼梯上遇到了邻居。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài lóutī shang yùdào le línjū.
examples.english: I ran into my neighbor on the stairs.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.
口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.

example.hanzi: 飞行员通过无线电呼叫塔台。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán tōngguò wúxiàndiàn hūjiào tǎtái.
example.english: The pilot called the control tower over the radio.
example.fact: 呼叫 stacks two "call out" verbs (呼, as in 呼喊; 叫, as in 叫喊) into one word. In the 20th century it picked up a specialized technical sense for calling over radio, telephone, or intercom (呼叫中心, "call center") — the older literal "to shout" sense and the newer telecom sense now coexist.

examples.hanzi: 他在山谷里大声呼叫，希望有人能听到。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shāngǔ lǐ dàshēng hūjiào, xīwàng yǒu rén néng tīngdào.
examples.english: He shouted loudly in the valley, hoping someone would hear.

examples.hanzi: 对方没有接听，系统会自动呼叫下一个号码。
examples.pinyin: Duìfāng méiyǒu jiētīng, xìtǒng huì zìdòng hūjiào xià yí ge hàomǎ.
examples.english: If the other party doesn't answer, the system automatically calls the next number.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 我很同情他的遭遇。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn tóngqíng tā de zāoyù.
example.english: I really sympathize with what happened to him.
example.fact: 同情 literally means "same (同) feeling (情)" — sharing another person's emotional state. That's the same root logic behind English "sympathy" (Greek syn- "together" + pathos "feeling"), a case where the Chinese and English etymologies for an abstract emotion line up almost exactly.

examples.hanzi: 大家都很同情这个受伤的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn tóngqíng zhège shòushāng de háizi.
examples.english: Everyone sympathized with the injured child.

examples.hanzi: 我不需要你的同情。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xūyào nǐ de tóngqíng.
examples.english: I don't need your sympathy.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 唉 is a sigh or exclamation.
矣 (yǐ) — loose sound hint (āi vs yǐ); same part in 挨 āi and 埃 āi.

example.hanzi: 唉,今天又要加班。
example.pinyin: Āi, jīntiān yòu yào jiābān.
example.english: Sigh, I have to work overtime again today.
example.fact: 唉 is a sigh of regret or resignation, often drawn out. 唉声叹气 is the idiom for sighing in distress. It can also be a quick reply meaning 'yes'. A rising or falling tone changes the mood.

examples.hanzi: 唉,我又忘了带雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Āi, wǒ yòu wàng le dài yǔsǎn.
examples.english: Ugh, I forgot my umbrella again.

examples.hanzi: 唉,这道数学题真难。
examples.pinyin: Āi, zhè dào shùxué tí zhēn nán.
examples.english: Sigh, this math problem is really hard.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.
日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; the sun over 京 gives a bright scene, hence scenery.
京 (jīng) gives the sound: 景 jǐng is close, as in 影 yǐng and 惊 jīng.

example.hanzi: 请介绍一下这个故事的背景。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jièshào yíxià zhège gùshi de bèijǐng.
example.english: Please introduce the background of this story.
example.fact: 背景 literally means "back (背) scenery (景)" — a term from theater staging and photography for whatever sits behind the main subject. It extended figuratively to mean both narrative "context" and, colloquially, a person's powerful hidden connections (有背景, "to have backing").

examples.hanzi: 你有什么文化背景？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme wénhuà bèijǐng?
examples.english: What is your cultural background?

examples.hanzi: 照片的背景是一座大山。
examples.pinyin: Zhàopiàn de bèijǐng shì yí zuò dà shān.
examples.english: The background of the photo is a big mountain.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.

example.hanzi: 我们通常六点下班。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen tōngcháng liù diǎn xiàbān.
example.english: We usually get off work at six o'clock.
example.fact: 下班 and 上班 ("to go to work") form a matched pair built on 班 ("shift, duty period" — the same 班 as in 班级, "school class"), with the directional opposites 上 ("up, into") and 下 ("down, out of") marking entering versus leaving one's post.

examples.hanzi: 你几点下班？我们一起走吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jǐ diǎn xiàbān? Wǒmen yìqǐ zǒu ba.
examples.english: What time do you get off work? Let's go together.

examples.hanzi: 下班后，他喜欢去健身房。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān hòu, tā xǐhuan qù jiànshēnfáng.
examples.english: After work, he likes to go to the gym.

components.note: 士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 她是一名护士。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng hùshi.
example.english: She is a nurse.
example.fact: 士 was the lowest rank of ancient nobility, then the scholar class, the first of the 士农工商 (scholar, farmer, artisan, merchant). Today it ends job and title words: 护士 (nurse), 博士 (doctorate), 战士 (soldier), 女士 (Ms.).

examples.hanzi: 这位博士在大学教书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi bóshì zài dàxué jiāoshū.
examples.english: This doctor teaches at the university.

examples.hanzi: 那位女士是我的老师。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi nǚshì shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: That lady is my teacher.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 有很多方法可以学中文,比如说看电视剧。
example.pinyin: Yǒu hěn duō fāngfǎ kěyǐ xué Zhōngwén, bǐrúshuō kàn diànshìjù.
example.english: There are many ways to learn Chinese, for example watching TV dramas.
example.fact: 比如说 tacks 说 ("to say") onto the simpler 比如 ("for example," itself from 比 "to compare" + 如 "as, like"). The two are functionally interchangeable — adding 说 just gives the phrase a slightly more spoken, conversational feel, similar to how English sometimes adds "say" as in "let's say, for example."

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢水果，比如说苹果和香蕉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, bǐrúshuō píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: I like fruit, for example apples and bananas.

examples.hanzi: 你可以做点运动，比如说跑步或者游泳。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zuò diǎn yùndòng, bǐrúshuō pǎobù huòzhě yóuyǒng.
examples.english: You could do some exercise, such as running or swimming.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 给, 经: cutting a thread, hence to break off.
色 (sè) is only a loose sound clue for jué.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 失去工作后,他感到很绝望。
example.pinyin: Shīqù gōngzuò hòu, tā gǎndào hěn juéwàng.
example.english: After losing his job, he felt very hopeless.
example.fact: 绝望 literally means "severed (绝) hope (望)." 绝 originally described cutting a thread completely through, so 绝望 pictures hope itself being cut clean through — a vivid escalation beyond just "having no hope" to hope being severed entirely.

examples.hanzi: 他对生活感到绝望。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì shēnghuó gǎndào juéwàng.
examples.english: He felt hopeless about life.

examples.hanzi: 别绝望，总会有办法的。
examples.pinyin: Bié juéwàng, zǒng huì yǒu bànfǎ de.
examples.english: Don't despair; there's always a way.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 她在大学学习法语。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí Fǎyǔ.
example.english: She studies French at university.
example.fact: 法语 abbreviates 法国 ("France") down to just 法 before adding 语 ("language") — the same one-character-country pattern seen throughout Chinese language names, e.g. 英语 (英 from 英国), 德语 (德 from 德国, also in this batch via 西德), and 俄语 (俄 from 俄罗斯, also in this batch).

examples.hanzi: 她的法语说得非常流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Fǎyǔ shuō de fēicháng liúlì.
examples.english: She speaks French very fluently.

examples.hanzi: 我想明年开始学法语。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng míngnián kāishǐ xué Fǎyǔ.
examples.english: I want to start learning French next year.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 请叫一辆救护车!
example.pinyin: Qǐng jiào yí liàng jiùhùchē!
example.english: Please call an ambulance!
example.fact: 救护车 is fully compositional: 救 ("to rescue," as in 救命 "help!") + 护 ("to protect, to nurse," as in 护士 "nurse") + 车 ("vehicle") — literally "rescue-and-care vehicle," a transparent three-character compound for a modern invention with no single native word before cars existed.

examples.hanzi: 快叫救护车，有人晕倒了！
examples.pinyin: Kuài jiào jiùhùchē, yǒu rén yūndǎo le!
examples.english: Call an ambulance quickly; someone has fainted!

examples.hanzi: 救护车很快就赶到了现场。
examples.pinyin: Jiùhùchē hěn kuài jiù gǎn dào le xiànchǎng.
examples.english: The ambulance arrived at the scene quickly.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.

example.hanzi: 这是一款全新的手机。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì kuǎn quánxīn de shǒujī.
example.english: This is a brand-new phone.
example.fact: 全新 intensifies 新 ("new") with 全 ("whole, entire") to mean "completely/brand new" — parallel to how English "brand-new" adds an intensifying word rather than leaning on "new" alone, a common Mandarin strategy for emphasis alongside totality words like 十分 or 完全.

examples.hanzi: 我们的新房子里，家具全是全新的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xīn fángzi lǐ, jiājù quán shì quánxīn de.
examples.english: The furniture in our new house is all brand new.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司打造了一个全新的品牌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī dǎzào le yí ge quánxīn de pǐnpái.
examples.english: This company built an entirely new brand.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 他的父母出生在西德。
example.pinyin: Tā de fùmǔ chūshēng zài Xī Dé.
example.english: His parents were born in West Germany.
example.fact: 西德 is a Cold War-era term for the Federal Republic of Germany (1949–1990), paired with its counterpart 东德 ("East Germany," the GDR). Since German reunification in 1990 both terms have become historical rather than current — modern Mandarin simply uses 德国 for unified Germany.

examples.hanzi: 他曾经在西德工作过几年。
examples.pinyin: Tā céngjīng zài Xī Dé gōngzuò guo jǐ nián.
examples.english: He once worked in West Germany for a few years.

examples.hanzi: 那堵墙把西德和东德分开了很多年。
examples.pinyin: Nà dǔ qiáng bǎ Xī Dé hé Dōng Dé fēnkāi le hěn duō nián.
examples.english: That wall separated West and East Germany for many years.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.

example.hanzi: 夏天出门要防晒。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān chūmén yào fángshài.
example.english: In summer you need sun protection when going out.
example.fact: 防 means to guard against: 预防 (to prevent), 防止 (to prevent), 防火 (fire prevention), 国防 (national defense). Product words use it too: 防水 (waterproof) and 防晒 (sunscreen).

examples.hanzi: 我们要预防感冒。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yùfáng gǎnmào.
examples.english: We need to prevent colds.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间装了防盗门。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān zhuāng le fángdàomén.
examples.english: This room has a security door installed.

components.note: 里 (village, land) — in 野 it means land: open country beyond the village, wild, as in 野兽.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 野 yě is close to 预 yù and 序 xù.

example.hanzi: 森林里有很多野生动物。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: There are many wild animals in the forest.
example.fact: 野 describes the wild or outdoors: 野生 (wild-growing), 野外 (outdoors), 野餐 (picnic), 田野 (fields). 野心 means ambition, sometimes with a negative edge. As an adjective it can also mean rough and untamed.

examples.hanzi: 他们在野外露营。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài yěwài lùyíng.
examples.english: They are camping in the wilderness.

examples.hanzi: 草地上开着一朵野花。
examples.pinyin: Cǎodì shang kāi zhe yì duǒ yěhuā.
examples.english: A wildflower is blooming on the grass.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 侠 is a chivalrous hero, as in 侠客 knight-errant.
夹 (jiā) — close sound: 侠 xiá. 夹 also sounds out 狭 xiá and 峡 xiá.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢看武侠小说。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn wǔxiá xiǎoshuō.
example.english: I like reading martial arts novels.
example.fact: 侠 is the wandering hero who upholds justice. The 武侠 (wuxia) genre, popularized by authors like 金庸 (Jin Yong), is built on this ideal. 大侠 is a great hero, and 侠义 means chivalry.

examples.hanzi: 这部武侠电影很精彩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù wǔxiá diànyǐng hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: This martial arts movie is very exciting.

examples.hanzi: 他像个大侠一样帮助别人。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng ge dàxiá yíyàng bāngzhù biérén.
examples.english: He helps others like a chivalrous hero.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 你能说说你的想法吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuōshuo nǐ de xiǎngfǎ ma?
example.english: Can you tell me a bit about your thoughts?
example.fact: 说说 reduplicates 说 ("to speak") in the AA pattern Mandarin uses for brief, low-commitment actions — the same pattern behind 看看 ("take a quick look") and 想想 ("think it over"). Reduplicating the verb softens a request, turning a bare imperative "speak!" into a gentler "just say a little."

examples.hanzi: 你先说说今天发生了什么。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān shuōshuo jīntiān fāshēng le shénme.
examples.english: First tell me what happened today.

examples.hanzi: 我们来说说下个月的计划吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen lái shuōshuo xià ge yuè de jìhuà ba.
examples.english: Let's talk about next month's plan.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and flowing things, as in 河, 海, 汤; 沮 originally meant to halt a flow, then to dishearten.
且 (qiě) hints at the sound: 沮 jǔ is close to 组 zǔ and 租 zū, which share it.
亡 (die, lose) — 丧 (simplified 喪) once showed crying 哭 over the dead 亡: mourning, then loss and dejection (沮丧).

example.hanzi: 考试没考好让他很沮丧。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì méi kǎohǎo ràng tā hěn jǔsàng.
example.english: Not doing well on the exam made him very dejected.
example.fact: 沮丧 pairs 沮 (whose 氵 water radical no longer connects clearly to dejection) with 丧, whose upper element pictures crying in mourning (from 哭). That mourning imagery anchors 沮丧's meaning a step beyond ordinary sadness, closer to a defeated, hope-drained gloom.

examples.hanzi: 他输了比赛，心情很沮丧。
examples.pinyin: Tā shū le bǐsài, xīnqíng hěn jǔsàng.
examples.english: He lost the game and felt dejected.

examples.hanzi: 别沮丧，下次一定会更好。
examples.pinyin: Bié jǔsàng, xià cì yídìng huì gèng hǎo.
examples.english: Don't be discouraged; next time will be better.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做, 作; 仿 is to imitate someone.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 仿 fǎng is close, as in 访 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 小孩子喜欢模仿父母的行为。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi xǐhuan mófǎng fùmǔ de xíngwéi.
example.english: Small children like to imitate their parents' behavior.
example.fact: 模仿 combines 模 ("mold, pattern," as in 模型 "model/mockup") with 仿 ("to copy, to resemble," as in 仿佛 "as if") — literally "to copy a mold," a concrete image standing in for the abstract act of imitation.

examples.hanzi: 鹦鹉会模仿人说话。
examples.pinyin: Yīngwǔ huì mófǎng rén shuō huà.
examples.english: Parrots can imitate human speech.

examples.hanzi: 他很会模仿名人的声音。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì mófǎng míngrén de shēngyīn.
examples.english: He is good at imitating celebrities' voices.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water, as in 海 sea, 河 river; 湖 is a lake.
胡 (hú) — same sound: 湖 hú. 胡 also sounds out 糊 hú and 蝴 hú.

example.hanzi: 湖里有很多鱼。
example.pinyin: Hú lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
example.english: There are many fish in the lake.
example.fact: 湖 names many famous lakes, like 西湖 in Hangzhou. The provinces 湖南 and 湖北 mean 'south of the lake' and 'north of the lake', after Dongting Lake. 江湖, 'rivers and lakes', is the wandering outsider world of wuxia stories.

examples.hanzi: 西湖是杭州有名的景点。
examples.pinyin: Xīhú shì Hángzhōu yǒumíng de jǐngdiǎn.
examples.english: West Lake is a famous sight in Hangzhou.

examples.hanzi: 我们在湖边散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài húbiān sànbù.
examples.english: We take a walk by the lake.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.hanzi: 我爸爸在一家律师事务所工作。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zài yì jiā lǜshī shìwùsuǒ gōngzuò.
example.english: My dad works at a law firm.
example.fact: 事务所 almost always attaches to a profession — most commonly 律师事务所 ("law firm," literally "lawyer affairs-office") and 会计师事务所 ("accounting firm"). It rarely stands alone in speech, functioning more like a suffix template for professional-services firms than a freestanding word for "office," for which 办公室 is the everyday term.

examples.hanzi: 我姐姐在一家会计事务所工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie zài yì jiā kuàijì shìwùsuǒ gōngzuò.
examples.english: My older sister works at an accounting firm.

examples.hanzi: 这家事务所专门处理房产问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shìwùsuǒ zhuānmén chǔlǐ fángchǎn wèntí.
examples.english: This firm specializes in real estate issues.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a roof over fire 火 means disaster; 宀 appears in 家 home, 安 safe.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.

example.hanzi: 这场洪水是一场巨大的灾难。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng hóngshuǐ shì yì chǎng jùdà de zāinàn.
example.english: This flood is a huge disaster.
example.fact: 灾难 combines 灾 (fire 火 breaking out under a roof 宀, per its own component breakdown) with 难 (originally "hard to catch a bird by hand," per its own component breakdown) — two independently vivid pictographic images of calamity reinforcing each other into one formal word for disaster.

examples.hanzi: 这次地震是一场可怕的灾难。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì dìzhèn shì yì chǎng kěpà de zāinàn.
examples.english: This earthquake was a terrible disaster.

examples.hanzi: 他们在灾难中失去了家园。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài zāinàn zhōng shīqù le jiāyuán.
examples.english: They lost their homes in the disaster.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand 爫 reaching down to a tree 木 to pick its fruit or leaves — to gather, as in 采访.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说, 语, 请; 访 is to visit and ask.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 访 fǎng is close, as in 仿 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 记者采访了这位科学家。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě cǎifǎng le zhè wèi kēxuéjiā.
example.english: The reporter interviewed this scientist.
example.fact: 采访 combines 采 ("to pick, to gather," pictured as a hand picking fruit from a tree) with 访 ("to visit, to call on") — journalism here is pictured as "gathering by visiting," a concrete metaphor for a reporter's fieldwork that predates the modern sense "to interview."

examples.hanzi: 电视台明天要采访这位老人。
examples.pinyin: Diànshìtái míngtiān yào cǎifǎng zhè wèi lǎorén.
examples.english: The TV station will interview this elderly man tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 接受采访时，她显得很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Jiēshòu cǎifǎng shí, tā xiǎnde hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: She looked nervous when being interviewed.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.

example.hanzi: 老师对他的作文评价很高。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì tā de zuòwén píngjià hěn gāo.
example.english: The teacher rated his essay very highly.
example.fact: 评价 combines 评 ("to comment, to judge," as in 评论 "commentary") with 价 ("value, price," as in 价格 "price") — literally "to judge the value of." English "to appraise" carries the same logic, tracing back to Latin appretiare, "to set a price on."

examples.hanzi: 大家对这家餐厅的评价很高。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhè jiā cāntīng de píngjià hěn gāo.
examples.english: Everyone rates this restaurant highly.

examples.hanzi: 你怎么评价这部电影？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme píngjià zhè bù diànyǐng?
examples.english: How do you evaluate this movie?

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 他 he, 们 plural, 住 live; 你 is "you".
尔 (ěr) is a loose sound clue for nǐ; 尔 also supplies 您 nín (polite you, with 心 added).
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 你家有几个人?
example.pinyin: Nǐjiā yǒu jǐ gè rén?
example.english: How many people are in your family?
example.fact: 你家 attaches the possessive 你 ("you") directly onto 家 ("home/family") with no linking word — Mandarin regularly drops 的 between a pronoun and a close relationship or possession, a compression that English's "your" + noun does not allow.

examples.hanzi: 我下午去你家找你，好吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ qù nǐ jiā zhǎo nǐ, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Shall I come to your place to see you this afternoon?

examples.hanzi: 你家离学校远不远？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā lí xuéxiào yuǎn bu yuǎn?
examples.english: Is your home far from school?

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 他相信正义终将战胜邪恶。
example.pinyin: Tā xiāngxìn zhèngyì zhōng jiāng zhànshèng xié'è.
example.english: He believes justice will ultimately triumph over evil.
example.fact: 正 already means "correct, upright" on its own (as in 正确, "correct"), and 义 means "righteousness, moral duty" — 正义 layers two near-synonymous "rightness" characters together, the same doubling strategy behind 喜欢 in the pilot batch.

examples.hanzi: 法律的目的是维护社会的正义。
examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ de mùdì shì wéihù shèhuì de zhèngyì.
examples.english: The purpose of law is to uphold justice in society.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个很有正义感的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn yǒu zhèngyìgǎn de rén.
examples.english: He is a person with a strong sense of justice.

components.note: 网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.
立 (stand) — the person-standing radical, as in 站 itself and 位 position; here it carries the meaning of standing.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound exactly: 站 zhàn, also in 战 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 这个网站的信息很有用。
example.pinyin: Zhège wǎngzhàn de xìnxī hěn yǒuyòng.
example.english: This website's information is very useful.
example.fact: 网站 is a modern coinage built from two older characters — 网 ("net," a woven hunting or fishing net) supplies the metaphor for a network, and 站 ("station," as in a bus or train stop) supplies the idea of a fixed point one arrives at — giving Chinese a compositional equivalent of "website" rather than a phonetic loanword.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在这个网站上订机票。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài zhège wǎngzhàn shang dìng jīpiào.
examples.english: You can book plane tickets on this website.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司的网站正在升级。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī de wǎngzhàn zhèngzài shēngjí.
examples.english: Our company's website is being upgraded.

meanings: (after a noun) place where it is located

components.note: 斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.hanzi: 这就是问题的所在。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiùshì wèntí de suǒzài.
example.english: This is exactly where the problem lies.
example.fact: 所 is a grammatical marker that turns a following verb into a noun-like "that which is [verb]ed" — attached to 在 ("to be located at"), 所在 literally means "that which is located," which is why it almost always trails a noun with 的 (问题的所在, "where the problem lies") rather than standing alone as an ordinary place word like 这里.

examples.hanzi: 他们找到了问题的所在。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhǎodào le wèntí de suǒzài.
examples.english: They found where the problem lies.

examples.hanzi: 这座古镇是文化遗产的所在地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔzhèn shì wénhuà yíchǎn de suǒzàidì.
examples.english: This ancient town is the site of cultural heritage.

components.note: 参 (cān) is a sound clue for 惨 cǎn and 掺 chān; the old shape pictured three stars.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 这位参议员支持这项新法律。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi cānyìyuán zhīchí zhè xiàng xīn fǎlǜ.
example.english: This senator supports this new law.
example.fact: 参议员 names a member of an upper legislative chamber generically — 参 ("to participate") + 议 ("to deliberate") + 员 ("member") — so it applies just as naturally to a U.S. senator as to a member of a "参议院" in another bicameral system, rather than being tied to one specific country.

examples.hanzi: 参议员明天会在会上发言。
examples.pinyin: Cānyìyuán míngtiān huì zài huì shang fāyán.
examples.english: The senator will speak at the meeting tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这位参议员已经工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi cānyìyuán yǐjīng gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
examples.english: This senator has served for twenty years.

components.note: 凶 (ominous) — an open pit 凵 with crossed marks inside: a trap, a sign of danger; seen in 凶手 murderer, 凶器 weapon.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 警察在现场找到了凶器。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài xiànchǎng zhǎodào le xiōngqì.
example.english: The police found the murder weapon at the scene.
example.fact: 凶 by itself means "fierce, ominous, deadly" (as in 凶手, "murderer"), and 器 means "tool, instrument" — 凶器 is a fully transparent compound, literally "a deadly tool," making it one of the easier crime-vocabulary words for a learner to reconstruct from its parts.

examples.hanzi: 警方还没有找到作案的凶器。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hái méiyǒu zhǎodào zuò'àn de xiōngqì.
examples.english: The police have not yet found the weapon used in the crime.

examples.hanzi: 那把刀可能就是凶器。
examples.pinyin: Nà bǎ dāo kěnéng jiùshì xiōngqì.
examples.english: That knife might be the murder weapon.

components.note: 尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 他被任命为新任局长。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi rènmìng wéi xīnrèn júzhǎng.
example.english: He was appointed as the new bureau chief.
example.fact: 长 (zhǎng, "head, chief") is a modular suffix that attaches to almost any organizational noun to name its leader — 局长 ("bureau chief"), 校长 ("school principal"), 部长 ("department minister") — all built the same way, so recognizing 长 as "the head of X" unlocks a whole family of job titles at once.

examples.hanzi: 局长明天要来视察。
examples.pinyin: Júzhǎng míngtiān yào lái shìchá.
examples.english: The bureau chief is coming for an inspection tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这位局长十分关心市民的生活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi júzhǎng shífēn guānxīn shìmín de shēnghuó.
examples.english: This bureau chief cares a lot about the citizens' lives.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and weaving, as in 红 red, 线 line, 细 fine; 绩 first meant spinning, then work achieved.
责 (zé) is only a loose sound hint for jì.

example.hanzi: 她这次考试的成绩很好。
example.pinyin: Tā zhè cì kǎoshì de chéngjì hěn hǎo.
example.english: Her grades on this exam are very good.
example.fact: 成绩 covers both a one-time test score and a longer-term track record of achievement — 这次考试的成绩 ("this exam's grade") and 工作成绩 ("job performance") use the exact same word, where English reaches for two different words, "grade" and "achievement/performance."

examples.hanzi: 你的成绩比上次进步了不少。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de chéngjì bǐ shàng cì jìnbù le bù shǎo.
examples.english: Your grades have improved a lot compared with last time.

examples.hanzi: 他在工作中取得了很大的成绩。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngzuò zhōng qǔdé le hěn dà de chéngjì.
examples.english: He has made great achievements in his work.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
灬 (fire) — the four-dot form of 火, as in 热 hot, 点 point, 煮 cook; 烈 is blazing, then intense.
列 (liè) gives the sound exactly: 烈 liè, also in 裂 liè (split).

example.hanzi: 大家对这个决定表示强烈反对。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège juédìng biǎoshì qiángliè fǎnduì.
example.english: Everyone expressed strong opposition to this decision.
example.fact: 强烈 almost always modifies an abstract noun or verb of feeling or reaction — 强烈反对 ("strong opposition"), 强烈的感情 ("intense feelings") — while for a person's or object's physical strength, Chinese instead reaches for the plainer 强壮 or 强大.

examples.hanzi: 她对猫有强烈的过敏反应。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì māo yǒu qiángliè de guòmǐn fǎnyìng.
examples.english: She has a strong allergic reaction to cats.

examples.hanzi: 我有一种强烈的感觉，今天会出事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì zhǒng qiángliè de gǎnjué, jīntiān huì chū shì.
examples.english: I have a strong feeling that something will happen today.

components.note: 网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.

example.hanzi: 我在网上买了一本书。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng mǎi le yì běn shū.
example.english: I bought a book online.
example.fact: 网 is a net, and in modern Chinese it means the internet: 上网 (go online), 网站 (website), 网购 (shop online), 网红 (internet celebrity). 网 is also a fishing net: 渔网.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢上网看视频。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan shàngwǎng kàn shìpín.
examples.english: He likes going online to watch videos.

examples.hanzi: 这里的网速很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhèli de wǎngsù hěn kuài.
examples.english: The internet speed here is very fast.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 他的沉默似乎意味着什么。
example.pinyin: Tā de chénmò sìhū yìwèizhe shénme.
example.english: His silence seemed to imply something.
example.fact: 意味 as a verb almost never stands alone — it takes the aspect suffix 着 to form 意味着 ("to signify, to imply"), one of the most common ways Chinese frames "X means/implies Y" in writing and speech alike.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息意味着我们要重新开始。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi yìwèizhe wǒmen yào chóngxīn kāishǐ.
examples.english: This news means we have to start over.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜有一种特别的意味。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài yǒu yì zhǒng tèbié de yìwèi.
examples.english: This dish has a special flavor.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 垒 is piling earth into a wall, as in 堡垒 fortress and 全垒打 home run.
厽 (lěi) — same sound: 垒 lěi. 厽 is three small piled blocks.

example.hanzi: 他们用石头垒了一道墙。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yòng shítou lěi le yí dào qiáng.
example.english: They built a wall out of stones.
example.fact: 垒 is to stack up stones or bricks: 垒墙 (build a wall). It builds 堡垒 (fortress) and baseball terms: 垒球 (softball), 一垒 (first base), 全垒打 (home run).

examples.hanzi: 孩子们用积木垒了一座塔。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yòng jīmù lěi le yí zuò tǎ.
examples.english: The kids built a tower out of blocks.

examples.hanzi: 他在棒球比赛中跑上了二垒。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bàngqiú bǐsài zhōng pǎo shàng le èr lěi.
examples.english: He ran to second base in the baseball game.

components.note: 壴 (zhù, drum) — a drum on top of 口 mouth: music and singing, joy.
口 (mouth) — singing and speaking, as in 唱 sing, 吃 eat.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 这部电影是一部很有趣的喜剧。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shì yí bù hěn yǒuqù de xǐjù.
example.english: This movie is a very funny comedy.
example.fact: 喜剧 pairs 喜 ("joy," the same character that doubles up in 喜欢 in the pilot batch) with 剧 ("drama, play") for a transparent "joyful drama" — its direct opposite, 悲剧 ("tragedy"), swaps in 悲 ("sorrow") for the exact same structure.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去看了一场喜剧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù kàn le yì chǎng xǐjù.
examples.english: We went to see a comedy on the weekend.

examples.hanzi: 他最喜欢的就是喜剧，因为看了让人开心。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuan de jiùshì xǐjù, yīnwèi kàn le ràng rén kāixīn.
examples.english: His favorite is comedy because it makes people happy.

components.note: 殳 (weapon, strike) — the radical of 段 and 毁; in 殿 it has no clear meaning, so just learn 殿 as palace hall (宫殿).
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 王子殿下今天将访问这座城市。
example.pinyin: Wángzǐ diànxià jīntiān jiāng fǎngwèn zhè zuò chéngshì.
example.english: His Royal Highness the prince will visit this city today.
example.fact: 殿下 literally means "below the palace hall" (殿, "palace hall" + 下, "below") — a self-effacing form of address that parallels 陛下 ("Your Majesty," literally "below the imperial steps") used for a reigning monarch, with 殿下 reserved for princes, princesses, and other highnesses one rank below.

examples.hanzi: 殿下，客人们已经到了。
examples.pinyin: Diànxià, kèrénmen yǐjīng dào le.
examples.english: Your Highness, the guests have arrived.

examples.hanzi: 公主殿下今天参加了开幕式。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzhǔ diànxià jīntiān cānjiā le kāimù shì.
examples.english: Her Highness the princess attended the opening ceremony today.

meanings: to go to teach a class

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and teaching, as in 说, 语, 读; 课 is a lesson.
果 (guǒ) hints at the sound: 课 kè is close to 颗 kē and 棵 kē, which share it.

example.hanzi: 我们八点开始上课。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bā diǎn kāishǐ shàngkè.
example.english: We start class at eight o'clock.
example.fact: 上 in 上课 carries the same "to engage with, to attend" sense as in 上班 ("to go to work") and 上网 ("to go online") — a single verb that turns whatever noun follows it into "to do the thing that noun is for," rather than its more literal meaning "to go up."

examples.hanzi: 今天下午三点上课，别迟到。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ sān diǎn shàngkè, bié chídào.
examples.english: Class starts at three this afternoon; don't be late.

examples.hanzi: 我在大学教书，每周上课十二个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài dàxué jiāo shū, měi zhōu shàngkè shí'èr ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I teach at a university and give twelve hours of classes a week.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — flowers and growth: 花, 草, 茶; 荣 (from 榮) is a tree 木 in full bloom: flourishing, honor.
言 (speech) — praise is spoken; the radical of 说 and 语 in its full form.
兴 (xīng) here stands in for an older sound part: the old form 譽 had 與 (yǔ), which gave yù.

example.hanzi: 获得这个奖项是一种荣誉。
example.pinyin: Huòdé zhège jiǎngxiàng shì yì zhǒng róngyù.
example.english: Winning this award is an honor.
example.fact: 荣 pictures grass 艹 and a tree 木 flourishing under cover, giving it the sense "to flourish, glory," while 誉 puts 言 ("speech") beside a growing 兴 ("to prosper") to mean "praise, reputation" — 荣誉 combines a picture of flourishing with a picture of praise into the abstract noun "honor."

examples.hanzi: 能代表国家参加比赛是一种荣誉。
examples.pinyin: Néng dàibiǎo guójiā cānjiā bǐsài shì yì zhǒng róngyù.
examples.english: It is an honor to represent the country in competitions.

examples.hanzi: 这个奖是对他多年努力的荣誉。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiǎng shì duì tā duō nián nǔlì de róngyù.
examples.english: This award is an honor for his many years of effort.

components.note: 尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; also in 常 cháng, 偿 cháng, 堂 táng. The old form showed 旨 "tasty".
尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; also in 常 cháng, 偿 cháng, 堂 táng. The old form showed 旨 "tasty".

example.hanzi: 你尝尝这个汤,看看咸不咸。
example.pinyin: Nǐ chángchang zhège tāng, kànkan xián bu xián.
example.english: Try this soup and see if it's salty enough.
example.fact: 尝尝 reduplicates the single verb 尝 ("to taste") to make the action feel small, casual, and low-commitment — "just a quick taste" — the exact same softening pattern behind 看看 ("take a quick look") and 试试 ("give it a try"), both cited in the pilot batch as models for this pattern.

examples.hanzi: 你尝尝这道菜，看看好不好吃。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chángchang zhè dào cài, kànkan hǎo bu hǎochī.
examples.english: Try this dish and see whether it tastes good.

examples.hanzi: 来，尝尝我做的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Lái, chángchang wǒ zuò de dàngāo.
examples.english: Here, have a taste of the cake I made.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 碗 is a bowl, first made of fired clay or stone.
宛 (wǎn) — same sound: 碗 wǎn. 宛 also sounds out 腕 wàn and 婉 wǎn.

example.hanzi: 请给我一碗米饭。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì wǎn mǐfàn.
example.english: Please give me a bowl of rice.
example.fact: 碗 is both a bowl and a measure word (一碗饭). 饭碗, a rice bowl, also means one's livelihood: 铁饭碗 ('iron rice bowl') is a secure job, once typically a state job.

examples.hanzi: 我吃了两碗面条。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī le liǎng wǎn miàntiáo.
examples.english: I ate two bowls of noodles.

examples.hanzi: 吃完饭,我来洗碗筷。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán fàn, wǒ lái xǐ wǎnkuài.
examples.english: After the meal, I'll wash the bowls and chopsticks.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and value: 财, 货, 买, 贵. 负 shows a person 人 carrying money: a burden, to bear or owe.

example.hanzi: 他要负责这个项目。
example.pinyin: Tā yào fùzé zhège xiàngmù.
example.english: He has to be responsible for this project.
example.fact: 负 builds 负责 (to be responsible), 负担 (burden), 负债 (to owe debt) and 负数 (negative number). 胜负 means win or lose, and 负 is the 'lost' side in a score. It is the opposite of 正 in many contexts.

examples.hanzi: 你要对自己的行为负责。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào duì zìjǐ de xíngwéi fùzé.
examples.english: You must take responsibility for your own actions.

examples.hanzi: 这个队赢了三场,负了一场。
examples.pinyin: Zhège duì yíng le sān chǎng, fù le yì chǎng.
examples.english: This team won three games and lost one.

components.note: 耂 (old) — shown in 老 old and 者; 考 first meant an aged person (the same word as 老), then to examine.
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound; also in 巧 qiǎo, 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 我明天考数学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān kǎo shùxué.
example.english: I have a math exam tomorrow.
example.fact: 考 is used both for taking and giving tests: 考试 (exam), 考虑 (to consider), 考古 (archaeology), 高考 (the national college entrance exam, a huge event in China), 考研 (to sit the graduate entrance exam).

examples.hanzi: 他考上了北京大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā kǎo shàng le Běijīng Dàxué.
examples.english: He got into Peking University.

examples.hanzi: 下周有汉语考试。
examples.pinyin: Xià zhōu yǒu Hànyǔ kǎoshì.
examples.english: There's a Chinese exam next week.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 她是一位很有名的设计师。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de shèjìshī.
example.english: She is a very famous designer.
example.fact: 师 is a modular suffix meaning "master, practitioner of a craft" that turns almost any skilled activity into a job title — 设计 ("to design") + 师 gives 设计师 ("designer"), the same pattern behind 老师 ("teacher") and 厨师 ("chef").

examples.hanzi: 这座楼是一位年轻的设计师设计的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lóu shì yí wèi niánqīng de shèjìshī shèjì de.
examples.english: This building was designed by a young designer.

examples.hanzi: 她想成为一名服装设计师。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng fúzhuāng shèjìshī.
examples.english: She wants to become a fashion designer.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 推; 挣 is to struggle, also to earn (zhèng).
争 (zhēng) gives the sound exactly: 挣 zhēng, also in 睁 zhēng.

example.hanzi: 他每个月挣一万块。
example.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè zhèng yí wàn kuài.
example.english: He earns ten thousand yuan a month.
example.fact: 挣钱 means to earn money, and 赚钱 means the same; 挣 is more colloquial. Read zhēng, 挣 means to struggle free, as in 挣扎 (to struggle) and 挣脱 (to break loose).

examples.hanzi: 他在餐馆打工挣钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cānguǎn dǎgōng zhèng qián.
examples.english: He earns money working part-time in a restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作挣得不多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò zhèng de bù duō.
examples.english: This job doesn't pay much.
